name: Jonathan
charge: Stripping himself of his robe for the man whom the Lord would make king; standing between his father and David’s innocent blood; thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee
summary: Jonathan’s soul was knit with David’s, and he loved him as his own soul; the same word describes the church, hearts knit together in love. The king’s son and heir stripped off his own robe and gave it to the shepherd, with his garments, his sword, his bow and his girdle. He warned David of his father’s intent, spoke good of him to Saul and had a javelin cast at him for it, and went out to him in the wood at Ziph to strengthen his hand in God. His loyalty exceeded his own desires, and the kindness he asked for reached his lame son at the king’s table.
offenseFull: When David had made an end of speaking to Saul, the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul; they made a covenant, and Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him and gave it to David, with his garments, even to his sword, his bow and his girdle (1 Samuel 18:1-4). Souls being knit is not speaking of anything unnatural between the two men. The same word describes the church, whose hearts are comforted by being knit together in love (Colossians 2:2), and the body, knit together by joints and bands (Colossians 2:19). Note the estate of the two men: Jonathan was the prince and the heir, David was an armourbearer out of Bethlehem, and a true friend does not rejoice in standing higher. A faithful friend is a strong defence and the medicine of life, and he that has found such a one has found a treasure (Ecclesiasticus 6:14).

Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants that they should kill David; the Philistines could not get him, so now the king wanted Israelites to kill an Israelite. But Jonathan delighted much in David and told him plainly that his father sought to kill him, and told him to take heed until the morning, abide in a secret place and hide himself (1 Samuel 19:1-7). Jonathan would have been next in line for the throne, and you would think his loyalty lay with his father, but he saw that the spirit was not on his father, it was on his brother David. Do not be ashamed to defend a friend, nor hide from him in the time of his trouble (Ecclesiasticus 22:25). He spoke good of David to Saul: let not the king sin against his servant, who had not sinned against him and whose works toward him had been very good, for he put his life in his hand and slew the Philistine and the Lord wrought a great salvation for all Israel, which Saul saw and rejoiced at; so why sin against innocent blood and slay David without a cause? The innocent and righteous are not to be slain (Exodus 23:7), and hands that shed innocent blood are among the things the Lord hates (Proverbs 6:16-17). Saul listened and swore that David would not be slain, and Jonathan brought him back. At the new moon, when David’s seat was empty and Jonathan covered for him, Saul’s anger was kindled against his own son, telling him that as long as the son of Jesse lived on the ground neither he nor his kingdom would be established, and he cast a javelin at him to smite him; by that Jonathan knew it was determined of his father to slay David (1 Samuel 20:30-33). He would not buy a throne with his friend’s blood. When David was hunted in the wilderness of Ziph, Jonathan rose up and went to him into the wood and strengthened his hand in God, telling him not to fear, for the hand of Saul his father would not find him, and David would be king over Israel and Jonathan would be next to him, and Saul his father knew it too (1 Samuel 23:16-17).
judgmentFull: Jonathan had asked that the kindness of the Lord continue toward his house and never be cut off from it (1 Samuel 20:12-17). The covenant outlived him. The Philistines followed hard after Saul and his sons and slew Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchi-shua on mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:2). David lamented over them in the spirit, a eulogy and a prophecy: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives and in their death they were not divided, swifter than eagles and stronger than lions; and

he was distressed for his brother Jonathan, whose love to him was wonderful, passing the love of women (2 Samuel 1:23-26). There is a friend that sticks closer than a brother (Proverbs 18:24); that is what Jonathan was. When David was king he asked whether any of the house of Saul was left, that he might show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake, fetched Mephibosheth, lame on both his feet, out of Lo-debar, restored him all the land of Saul, and set him at the king’s table continually (2 Samuel 9:1-13). When seven of Saul’s house were delivered to the Gibeonites, the king spared Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan because of the oath of the Lord that was between them (2 Samuel 21:7). Jonathan did not live to stand next to David, but his bones were gathered with his father’s into the sepulchre of Kish (2 Samuel 21:12-14), and the kindness he asked for was still being served at the king’s table years after he died.

text.text: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
And Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father’s house.
Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.

That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ;
And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.
A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found such an one hath found a treasure.
And Saul spake to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should kill David.

But Jonathan Saul’s son delighted much in David: and Jonathan told David, saying, Saul my father seeketh to kill thee: now therefore, I pray thee, take heed to thyself until the morning, and abide in a secret place, and hide thyself:
And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where thou art, and I will commune with my father of thee; and what I see, that I will tell thee.

And Jonathan spake good of David unto Saul his father, and said unto him, Let not the king sin against his servant, against David; because he hath not sinned against thee, and because his works have been to thee-ward very good:

For he did put his life in his hand, and slew the Philistine, and the Lord wrought a great salvation for all Israel: thou sawest it, and didst rejoice: wherefore then wilt thou sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause?
And Saul hearkened unto the voice of Jonathan: and Saul sware, As the Lord liveth, he shall not be slain.
And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan shewed him all those things. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence, as in times past.
I will not be ashamed to defend a friend; neither will I hide myself from him.
Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.
These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:
A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,

Then Saul’s anger was kindled against Jonathan, and he said unto him, Thou son of the perverse rebellious woman, do not I know that thou hast chosen the son of Jesse to thine own confusion, and unto the confusion of thy mother’s nakedness?
For as long as the son of Jesse liveth upon the ground, thou shalt not be established, nor thy kingdom. Wherefore now send and fetch him unto me, for he shall surely die.
And Jonathan answered Saul his father, and said unto him, Wherefore shall he be slain? what hath he done?
And Saul cast a javelin at him to smite him: whereby Jonathan knew that it was determined of his father to slay David.
And Jonathan Saul’s son arose, and went to David into the wood, and strengthened his hand in God.
And he said unto him, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee; and that also Saul my father knoweth.

And Jonathan said unto David, O Lord God of Israel, when I have sounded my father about to morrow any time, or the third day, and, behold, if there be good toward David, and I then send not unto thee, and shew it thee;

The Lord do so and much more to Jonathan: but if it please my father to do thee evil, then I will shew it thee, and send thee away, that thou mayest go in peace: and the Lord be with thee, as he hath been with my father.
And thou shalt not only while yet I live shew me the kindness of the Lord, that I die not:
But also thou shalt not cut off thy kindness from my house for ever: no, not when the Lord hath cut off the enemies of David every one from the face of the earth.
So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, Let the Lord even require it at the hand of David’s enemies.
And Jonathan caused David to swear again, because he loved him: for he loved him as he loved his own soul.
And the Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi–shua, Saul’s sons.
Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.
Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with other delights, who put on ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, thou wast slain in thine high places.
I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?
And there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name was Ziba. And when they had called him unto David, the king said unto him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.
And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, which is lame on his feet.
And the king said unto him, Where is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo–debar.
Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lo–debar.
Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come unto David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!

And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
And he bowed himself, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I am?
Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said unto him, I have given unto thy master’s son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.

Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in the fruits, that thy master’s son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master’s son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king’s sons.
And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name was Micha. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants unto Mephibosheth.
So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king’s table; and was lame on both his feet.
But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the Lord’s oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh–gilead, which had stolen them from the street of Beth–shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa:
And he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.

And the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was intreated for the land.
The envious man hath a wicked eye; he turneth away his face, and despiseth men.
